teaser: Anthropic's Scion replaced Git for agents inside one company; sgit, open source and encrypted, shares its core ideas from the other direction. Measured.
core_idea: Agents broke Git's offline, full-clone assumptions at Anthropic, which built Scion: a server that does history, blame, merges and commits, immutable objects served from cache tiers, and clients that fetch only what they need; sgit reaches the same properties from the opposite design, a dumb server that stores encrypted objects named by their ciphertext, reads from any static host or CDN, and scoped, shallow and on-demand clones, measured on 0.22.0; Scion is ahead on server-side history, merge, blame and proven scale, but it is internal, while sgit is open source and encrypts everything.

nodes.label: Scion: the server does the work
nodes.summary: History, blame, merges server-side; cache tiers; no full copy.

nodes.label: sgit: a dumb, blind server
nodes.summary: Client encrypts, merges and verifies; server stores ciphertext.

nodes.label: Immutable ids that cache
nodes.summary: SHA-256 of the ciphertext; served immutable for a year.

nodes.label: Reads from any GET host
nodes.summary: --transport static; no sgit server in the path.

nodes.label: Measured on 0.22.0
nodes.summary: Scoped clone 4 s against 59; static host clone identical.

nodes.label: Where Scion is ahead
nodes.summary: Server-side merge, blame, bisect; proven scale; no packing in sgit.

nodes.label: Git side by side
nodes.summary: Coexist in a folder; no history bridge.

nodes.label: Internal versus open
nodes.summary: Scion unreleased; sgit on PyPI today.
